baseline.what: Average dose equivalent measured on the lunar surface by the Lunar Lander Neutrons and Dosimetry (LND) experiment on China's Chang'e 4 lander (Jan-Feb 2019, solar minimum). About 2.6x the galactic-cosmic-ray dose inside the ISS.

source.title: Zhang et al. 2020, First measurements of the radiation dose on the lunar surface, Science Advances 6:eaaz1334

iss_comparison.what: Inside the ISS in the same weeks: 523 microsieverts a day from cosmic rays alone (the figure Zhang 2020 compares with, 1369/523 = about 2.6), or 731 including the South Atlantic Anomaly.

source.title: Zhang et al. 2020 (DOSIS 3D DOSTEL on the ISS, same period)

limits.what: NASA's career radiation limit for astronauts is 600 mSv.

source.title: NASA NTRS 20230012405, Biological Space Radiation Countermeasures to Enable Long Duration Exploration Missions

limits.context: Astronauts are exposed to effective doses from 50 to 2,000 mSv; 1 mSv is about 10 chest x-rays.

shielding.what: Solar-flare protons are stopped well by mass: regolith, water, or packed supplies. Covering a base with Moon soil is an idea NASA has studied, not a current plan. Galactic cosmic rays are much harder to stop.

sources.title: NASA NTRS 19890004839, Solar-flare shielding with regolith at a lunar-base site
NASA NTRS 20110012713, Radiation shielding of lunar regolith/polyethylene composites and regolith/water mixtures

game.time_scale_note: The mission is a real 10 days. The dose numbers are scaled up so choices matter in 10 days.
game.mission_limit_note: Game limit for this one 10-day mission: 1/12 of NASA's 600 mSv career limit. Doing nothing for 10 days costs ~27 game-mSv; one big storm without shelter pushes you over.
game.shields_note: PRETEND TECH: no NASA design uses powered radiation shields; mass, not electricity, blocks radiation. In the game, power to 'shields' stands for pumping water walls around the crew area; it cuts the dose rate by up to 50% at a 30% share.
game.shelter_note: Modelled on Orion's shelter: up to 24 h inside, then the crew must rest 12 h; storm dose x0.25 (Artemis I measured about 4x less in the best-shielded spot), cosmic-ray dose x0.7 (game assumption). No science or rover work in the shelter.

pretend_tech.shields: powered water-wall pumps (mass blocks radiation, not electricity)
pretend_tech.greenhouse: a working greenhouse at the outpost (a future idea)
pretend_tech.relay: the relay satellite (NASA plans a lunar relay network; none is working yet)

game.dose_scale_note: Game doses are doubled so storms matter in 10 days.

shelter_real.what: Orion's real storm shelter: the HERA sensor gives up to 1 h of warning; the crew pack into the floor bays behind stowage bags and can stay up to 24 h. On Artemis I the best-shielded spot got about 4x less dose.

sources.title: DLR: Orion radiation protection tested, Artemis I findings (2024)
